name: Rocket from the Crypt
label: Headhunter
lede: Six people in matching outfits let a game show wheel pick the setlist, and anyone with the logo tattooed on their body gets in free for life.

eras.title: Out of the ashes of Pitchfork
eras.text: John Reis pulls a new band out of the wreckage of Pitchfork, gives everyone a stage name and has them in matching outfits before the first record is out. The horns follow almost at once.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Wikipedia: John Reis
years.h: Pitchfork ends, and Reis borrows a name from a dead band
years.p: John Reis, now "Speedo", takes the name from the defunct 1970s punk band [[Rocket from the Tombs|3ce68b60-1c6c-4b0f-87fd-0f13410df01d]]. The first line-up lasts about six months.
years.xp:
Reis had formed Pitchfork at 17 with [[Rick Froberg|07d99b38-fa92-4916-a190-1240b1d2e402]] and played guitar until it dissolved in 1990. He and Froberg went straight on to [[Drive Like Jehu|608c9da7-d3ef-4661-828b-24bb6ae20cd6]], while Reis started Rocket from the Crypt on the side.

The first line-up was Reis, Andy Stamets, Pete Reichert, a drummer named Sean and backing vocalist Elaina. Sean and Elaina both left San Diego within months.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography · Trouser Press: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Paint as a Fragrance, HED #003
years.p: San Diego's Headhunter label puts out the first album, by a line-up that won't last the year. Trouser Press panned the sleeve.

years.cap: The band in matching shirts and checkered ties at Club 860
years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: A drummer called Atom and a sax player called Apollo 9
years.p: Adam Willard becomes "Atom", Andy Stamets "ND" and Pete Reichert "Petey X". Paul O'Beirne joins on sax as "Apollo 9".
years.xp:
The band dressed alike and borrowed from 1950s to 1970s garage, rock and soul acts. Encyclopedia.com says Reis added the sax after hearing Stax 45s.

They also made their own lyric booklets and handed out noisemakers, which is where the show-band reputation starts.

eras.title: Fans become billboards
eras.text: The band records in Los Angeles during the riots, fans start getting the logo tattooed for free entry, and Interscope signs Reis with room left to put out vinyl elsewhere.

years.src: Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt · Trouser Press: Rocket from the Crypt · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography
years.h: Circa: Now! gets cut while Los Angeles riots
years.p: Headhunter HED #015, recorded during the Rodney King riots, with videos for "Sturdy Wrists" and "Ditch Digger".
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com places the sessions in Los Angeles in 1992, during the riots that followed the Rodney King verdict. The album came out on Headhunter first and was picked up by Interscope and Atlantic in 1993.

years.cap: The singer-guitarist at the mic, Club 860, December 4, 1992
years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · ABC News: Rocket From the Crypt Takes Off · San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Get the logo tattooed, get in free for life
years.p: By 2001, ABC News counted more than 3,000 people with the logo, about 450 of them in San Diego. Wikipedia says Reis announced the deal in a fanzine.
years.xp:
Reis has told it differently. In that 2001 ABC News piece he said it started when friends of the band got tattooed and landed on guest lists: "We really can't take credit for masterminding it", and it was "perpetuated by people who were into us, not by us preaching this gospel of tattoos".

Free admission has a cost. Reis told ABC, "There are a couple of gigs where it gets a little hard to pull it off." MTV VJ Kennedy showed the band tattoo on national television during the Interscope years.

years.cap: At the mic at Club 860, December 4, 1992
years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Interscope signs two Reis bands in one deal
years.p: Rocket from the Crypt and Drive Like Jehu sign together at the end of 1992, and Reis stays free to release vinyl elsewhere.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the deal to 1992 and Encyclopedia.com to the end of 1992. One band was a horn-driven show band and the other a fractured post-hardcore four-piece, and now they shared a label.

The vinyl carve-out is why the next few years are full of small-label singles and EPs.

years.src: Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Trouser Press: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: MTV plays "Ditch Digger", and the horns get a trumpet
years.p: Jason Crane takes the trumpet chair as "JC 2000".
years.xp: Sources disagree on when he joined. Wikipedia's text says 1992, its member table 1994, and Trouser Press and Encyclopedia.com say 1993. This page uses 1993.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Trouser Press: Rocket from the Crypt
yt: The band shows you around San Diego, March 1994
years.h: Reis spends six months on Yank Crime instead
years.p: Rocket from the Crypt takes a break while Reis records Drive Like Jehu's second album. Cargo, Interscope and Atlantic release it.

eras.title: A game show wheel and a British hit
eras.text: Interscope pays for a tour with no cover charge, a game show wheel picks the setlist, and "On a Rope" lands on Top of the Pops. The follow-up arrives at a label that has moved on.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt · Trouser Press: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: A new record on Perfect Sound, then six weeks with no cover
years.p: Hot Charity comes out on Perfect Sound, and Interscope pays for a tour with no admission charged.
years.xp:
Encyclopedia.com says the vinyl run was 5,000 copies. It followed the two-track The State of Art Is on Fire EP, a vinyl-only release on Sympathy for the Record Industry that April.

Wikipedia describes the Interscope-backed free tour as running six weeks.

years.src: Wikipedia: Scream, Dracula, Scream! · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Trouser Press: Rocket from the Crypt
yt: "On a Rope" and "Born in '69" on The White Room, 22 December 1995
years.h: Scream, Dracula, Scream! brings strings and a real budget
years.p: Reis produces it himself, and the basic tracks go down live on a 4-track machine in about two months.
years.xp:
Videos were shot for "On a Rope", "Born in '69" and "Young Livers". Wikipedia notes the record was built on a bigger budget with string sections.

Reis later had mixed feelings about the strings: "Conceptually it was a great idea but I didn't really think it was working."

years.cap: Ticket stub for Rancid and Rocket from the Crypt at Roseland, New York, March 28, 1996
years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt
yt: Full set at Coney Island High, New York, August 1997
years.h: A game show wheel picks the setlist
years.p: Shows come with raffles, fire breathing and matching outfits, and the wheel decides what gets played next.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Wikipedia: Scream, Dracula, Scream!
years.h: Top of the Pops gets a six-piece in matching outfits
years.p: "On a Rope" enters the UK chart at No. 12, and the NME Awards give the band the Phillip Hall Radar award.
years.xp: An American punk band with a sax player and matching outfits was suddenly on MTV Europe and Top of the Pops. The band toured the US, UK and Europe, supporting Rancid and Soundgarden and headlining their own dates.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt · San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Interscope looks elsewhere after RFTC
years.p: Kevin Shirley produces it, and "Break It Up" and "Lipstick" get radio play, but sales fall short.
years.xp: Wikipedia says album sales underperformed and Interscope shifted focus to bigger sellers; the San Diego Reader says the label ignored the band. Chris Prescott of Tanner and No Knife toured with the band on percussion and keyboards.

eras.title: Leaving on Halloween
eras.text: Drummer Adam Willard quits, Interscope drifts off, and Reis spends his time on Hot Snakes, Sultans and his own label, Swami. On Halloween 2005 he calls the band off.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Wikipedia: John Reis
years.h: Cut Carefully and Play Loud is a stopgap on Flapping Jet
years.p: The EP comes out the same year SLAMM magazine names the band the best San Diego band of all time.
years.xp: Swami, Reis's own San Diego label, put out the rarities collection All Systems Go 2 that October. Wikipedia lists Reis's new bands Hot Snakes and Sultans as starting around the same time.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Atom Willard quits, and the Interscope years end
years.p: The drummer leaves after disagreements about direction, then goes on to Weezer's crew, the Offspring and Angels & Airwaves.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · ABC News: Rocket From the Crypt Takes Off
years.h: A pro skater takes the drum stool for Group Sounds
years.p: Superchunk's Jon Wurster fills in on the early sessions, then Mario Rubalcaba, now "Ruby Mars", takes over. Vagrant releases it.
years.xp: The band hadn't toured for two and a half years when it set out to promote the record. ABC News reported two shows a day for the first two weeks. Reis described the plan: "During the day, we'll be playing at free shows at record stores."

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography · Magnet: Rocket From The Crypt, Speedo's Army
years.h: Live from Camp X-Ray is the last studio album
years.p: Reis calls it "a fairly mundane punk record".

years.q: The official reason for the split
years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Magnet: Rocket From The Crypt, Speedo's Army · Wikipedia: R.I.P. (Rocket from the Crypt album) · Encyclopedia.com: Rocket from the Crypt · San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Halloween 2005, and Reis leaves the stage as a witch doctor
years.p: El Vez hosts 25 songs for a capacity crowd in the Westin ballroom. Reis enters on a gurney.
years.xp:
That reason is a joke. His real one, per Wikipedia, was that he could no longer sustain the "strenuous, military-like" practice the band demanded, and anything less would be a different band.

The show was filmed. Wikipedia and Magnet both say the Westin; Encyclopedia.com and the San Diego Reader place it at the Casbah.

eras.title: Buried, sort of
eras.text: The band is dead, but a DVD, some compilations and a children's TV show keep it moving. Reis has other plans.

years.src: Wikipedia: R.I.P. (Rocket from the Crypt album) · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt discography
years.h: R.I.P. puts the farewell on CD and DVD
years.p: Vagrant releases it in 2008, two years after a rough cut circulated on Swami.
years.xp: The rough cut, RFTC 10/31/05, came out on Swami in October 2006. A fire at the video production company Fourth Project delayed the final version. Pitchfork rated it 7.6.

years.src: Wikipedia: John Reis · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Reis starts over with the Night Marchers
years.p: Their first album, See You in Magic, comes out in April 2008.
years.xp:
Reis had played in Sultans until the band broke up in January 2007. Petey X started Merch Lackey. Apollo 9 teaches project management and marketing at a San Diego high school. JC 2000 moved to Belize. Ruby Mars co-owns Thirsty Moon Records.

Reis said in 2008, "I do have a little regret in that now that we don't play together I don't see those guys anymore."

years.cap: John Reis singing and playing guitar at Groezrock, Belgium
years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt · Punknews: Rocket from the Crypt, He's a Chef
yt: "He's a Chef" on Yo Gabba Gabba
years.h: A children's TV show gets the band back together
years.p: Atom Willard is back on drums for "He's a Chef" on Yo Gabba Gabba!, released only through Volcom stores.

years.big: I thought that was it and I never wanted to play those fucking songs ever again.
years.src: LA Record: Rocket from the Crypt, Yes to Everything · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Reis announces a full reunion anyway
years.p: He told the LA Record in 2014 that he had thought the 2005 farewell was the end.
years.xp: Fan demand changed his mind. Continuing to say no "seemed ridiculous" when people wanted to see them, he said, and he kept the plan loose: "This could end after these shows or it could go on."

eras.title: Back from the crypt
eras.text: Halloween shows become a ritual, festivals in Chicago and Belgium book the band, and old tapes keep turning up.

years.cap: The sax in an embroidered western shirt at Groezrock, Belgium, April 27, 2013
years.src: San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt · setlist.fm: Rocket From the Crypt at Riot Fest Chicago 2013
years.h: Riot Fest puts the band in Humboldt Park
years.p: The September set comes in the reunion's first year back, on a run of dates across the US, Europe and Australia.
years.xp: The band had played Groezrock in Belgium that April. On October 31 it played a House of Blues Halloween show in San Diego, the start of an annual tradition that continues to this day.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Sonny Vincent gets the band behind him on Vintage Piss
years.p: The sessions date from 2003 and sat unmixed until Reis finished and produced the record after the reunion. It comes out in March 2015.

years.cap: Rocket from the Crypt live in Chicago
years.src: San Diego Reader: Free Rocket From the Crypt tattoos
years.h: Mayo Maggiore sets up free rocket tattoos at the Halloween show
years.p: The tattooer, who inked Reis backstage at a Hot Snakes show in Milan in 2018, does free flash before the set.
years.xp: Maggiore got through eight flashes in about two and a half hours. The Pushead-designed logo was the best seller, and the San Diego Reader says the Halloween free tattoos have become an annual thing.

years.src: San Diego Reader: Rocket from the Crypt · Wikipedia: Rocket from the Crypt
years.h: Group Sounds front to back at Riot Fest
years.p: Rocket from the Crypt play the whole 2001 album in Chicago on September 16.

years.src: Loudwire: Rocket From The Crypt Found Lost Masters Online
years.h: A fan spots the master tapes on OfferUp
years.p: The fan tells the band, and Reis buys the tapes at liquidation auctions and spends months restoring them.
years.xp:
The tapes hold The State of Art Is on Fire EP and, to Reis's surprise, almost all of Scream, Dracula, Scream!. He used a reptile egg incubator to keep the tape from degrading, and told Loudwire he was relieved: "I was quite nervous of a very real possibility of uncovering nothing but banter and fart noises." The early recordings are set for release as Scream, Frankenstein, Scream!

Vinyl is sold only at five shows: Warsaw in New York on October 15, Irving Plaza in New York on October 16, the Metro in Chicago on October 17, House of Blues in San Diego on October 24 and the Electric Ballroom in London on November 7.
